title: Take a pack from the back of a chest freezer whose lid is stopped part open by a wall cupboard
instruction: Take the blue pack out of the freezer and put it on the grey mat.
context: Done by: cooks, food preparation workers and stockers (O*NET 35-2014, 35-2021, 53-7065). A chest freezer under a wall cupboard opens only part way, so stock at the back is reached under the lid with the hand angled; straight down, the wrist goes 20 mm into the lid. A look-alike white pack beside it means the pack is picked by colour, as stock is by label. Unlike TK-3E7BYW (slide a tray out from under a pass) and TK-HQMFVH (a case leans, not the hand), the hand must enter at an angle.
setup: World frame for this text: 'in front' is away from the arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, heights are above the table top, and the midline is halfway between the two arm bases (61 cm apart). Freezer (fixed, white): an open box 240 mm front to back and 280 mm wide, its front face 23 cm in front of the arm bases, its right side 6 cm right of the midline and its left side 22 cm left of it; walls 120 mm tall and 15 mm thick, floor 20 mm thick, so the inside is 210 x 250 mm and 100 mm deep. Lid: a pale blue panel 240 x 280 x 12 mm hinged along its top back edge (132 mm up, over the back wall), with a grey handle bar 120 x 15 x 20 mm along its front edge. It hangs on a counterbalance hinge: a grey weighted arm 120 mm deep, 280 mm wide and 70 mm tall behind the hinge, out of sight under the cupboard; lid, handle and arm together 1.0 kg. The counterbalance swings the lid up until its top face meets an orange rubber bumper on the cupboard's lower front edge, at 47 degrees open: the lid's front edge is then 31 cm up and 31 cm in front of the arm bases. Wall: a beige board 20 mm thick, 500 mm wide and 400 mm tall standing on the table, its front face 61.5 cm in front of the arm bases (14.5 cm behind the freezer). Wall cupboard (fixed, grey): a box from the wall forward to 39.6 cm in front of the arm bases (219 mm deep), 300 mm wide (1 cm past each side of the freezer) and 140 mm tall, sitting on the bumper, a 12 x 12 mm orange strip along its lower front edge whose underside is 211 mm up. Two packs (loose, rigid, 60 mm front to back, 45 mm wide, 50 mm tall, 0.1 kg each), one blue and one white, stand on the freezer floor near the back, centred 39.5 cm in front of the arm bases (back faces 30 mm from the inside of the back wall), one at 13 cm and one at 3 cm left of the midline; the lid's underside is 93 to 157 mm above their tops. Grey mat: 120 x 120 x 4 mm, flat on the table, centred 30 cm in front and 36 cm left of the midline. Lot A: blue pack at 13 cm left, white at 3 cm. Lot B swaps the two packs. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Judged at the end of each trial, after the robot has let go (no gripper within 5 mm of either pack) and with both packs still. 1.0: the blue pack rests on the grey mat (its lowest point within 1 mm of the mat's top, its centre over the mat) and the white pack is still in the freezer (its centre inside the freezer's inside walls and below the rim). 0.5: the white pack still in the freezer, and the blue pack out of the freezer, wholly clear of its outer footprint and resting on the table (lowest point within 1 mm of the table or of the mat's top), but its centre not over the mat. 0 otherwise: the blue pack left in the freezer, on the rim or the lid, still held, or off the table; or the white pack out of the freezer, whatever happened to the blue one. A trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s. Trials are run on each of lots A and B and averaged.
reset_notes: Put both packs back upright on the freezer floor at the back (lot A: blue at 13 cm left of the midline, white at 3 cm; lot B: swapped), and let the lid rise back against the cupboard. Nothing is consumed. Run with -E object_jitter=0 and --epochs 2.
fidelity: Bench scale: what is reproduced is the reach under the lid, a pack 30 mm from the back wall with the lid stopped 47 degrees open, 93 to 157 mm above the pack tops. The freezer itself is smaller than a real one (24 cm deep, 12 cm tall). The counterbalance hinge is a weighted arm; real ones use springs. The lid can be pushed down, not lifted further. Packs are rigid with no frost sticking; friction is a simulator value. The lots stop a fixed left or right habit, not a memorised replay.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A and B); demo: 1.0 in each lot
